This doesn’t mean that a peer led ceremony is unstructured or that there are no rules. It would be a very pure way of learning to have a ceremony with a bunch of altered people trying to figure out the rules as they go along, but I wouldn’t recommend it. There needs to be screening, sober sitters, emergency plans, integration, etc.

Membership, land, resources, governance, kids, leaving, etc.

I’m personally moving towards communities with less and less money involved. I think this will happen in stages.

First there will be no money exchanged between members for basic community functions like food, housing, care, tools, education, transport etc. Members might have outside jobs and bring their income in (in some agreed amount). This is probably where I’d want to start if I were starting a community.
e21-emuB:
This doesn’t mean that these ceremonies should be done without structure. Things like screening participants, making sure the sitters are sober, having a plan for dealing with emergencies, thinking about integration, and other rules and boundaries need to be dealt with beforehand. While there may be some pure learning that could come from having several altered members figure out what rules and boundaries are needed on the spot, it’s not something I recommend.

Membership, land, resources, governance, kids, leaving, etc.

I believe that eventually I will want to be part of a community that uses less and less money. I see this happening in stages:

1. Nothing is bought or sold within the community. Everything needed for life in the community (food, housing, care, tools, education, transportation, etc.) is provided within the community. If members work outside the community they bring their money in, but the money they bring in is agreed upon beforehand. This is probably a good place to start if someone wants to create a community now and have it be realistic.
